CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
JUNE 28, 2016
   City Manager Prichard provided a brief staff report (as per agenda material).

  Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a brief summary of overall
  revenues and expenditures (as per agenda material).

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN noted some minor corrections.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that two City cars are set to be replaced and
  suggested looking into the possibility of leasing. Administrative Services Director
  Whitehead stated that discussion has taken place regarding the value of leasing
  versus purchasing, which may make sense for the sedan, but probably would not
  be a viable option for the maintenance vehicles. He further noted that they will
  also look into hybrid models for the sedan.

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN commended the staff for utilizing their cars for so many
  years.

  Pam Schachter, 46 Ranchview Road, requested clarification regarding the
  increased amount listed under administration and support for personnel.
  Administrative Services Director Whitehead, City Manager Prichard and MAYOR
  PRO TEM ZERUNYAN explained comprehensively the issue of the PERS actuarial
  analysis and the resulting increase, which is programmed for pay-off during
  FY16-17 pending formal action by the COUNCIL at the next meeting.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN commented on the City’s outstanding financial
  position, and commended the department heads for their work in completing
  projects over the past few years and proposing for the future a large number of
  major projects. He also commended the staff’s efforts to apply for and receive
  various grants.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that while the City currently has increased
  revenues, the ups and downs of certain key revenues require COUNCIL to be
  prudent in managing those funds. She further noted her hope that improvements
  underway in the commercial district will enhance the City’s sales tax revenue.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  MAYOR PRO  TEM  ZERUNYAN  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCILWOMAN
  MITCHELL

  TO ADOPT THE FUND BALANCE POLICY, INVESTMENT POLICY, FISCAL
  YEAR 2016-17 BUDGET, FISCAL YEAR 2016-17 FEES AND CHARGES,
  AND ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 2379 ADOPTING THE CONSOLIDATED
  BUDGET, AND RESOLUTION NO. 2381 ESTABLISHING THE SCHEDULE
  OF MUNICIPAL FEES AND CHARGES; AND APPROVE SELECTING THE
  CHANGE IN CALIFORNIA PER CAPITA PERSONAL INCOME CHANGE
  DATE AS THE INFLATION FACTOR FOR THE FISCAL YEAR 2016-17;
  SELECTING THE GROWTH OF THE COUNTY AS THE POPULATION
  FACTOR FOR FISCAL YEAR 2016-17; AND ADOPT RESOLUTION NO.
  2380 ESTABLISHING THE FISCAL YEAR APPROPRIATION LIMIT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

  City Manager Prichard read Resolution Nos. 2379, 2380 and 2381 by title only.

  MINUTES OF JUNE 20, 2016.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL referred to the City Celebration which will be held
  at Howlett Park on September 17 and thanked Commissioner Schachter, and the
  Park and Activities Commission, for their work in coordinating this event.

C.  MC GOWAN CONSULTING LLC PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT FOR
  MS4 PERMIT CONSULTING SERVICES

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Professional Services
  Agreement with McGowan Consulting LLC for MS4 Permit compliance assistance
  for FY 2016-17 in an amount not to exceed $88,800.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL inquired as to how the City will be able to comply
  with all of the MS4 Permit requirements.

  Ms. McGowan responded that the Enhanced Watershed Management Program
  (EWMP) and Integrated Waste Management Plan (IWMP) are expected to
  implement the measures as cited and that the challenge is meeting the required
  deadlines. Discussion ensued regarding Machado Lake and the City of Torrance
  projects that might include the Peninsula in hopes of reducing costs.

  In response to MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN, Ms. McGowan noted that cost
  estimates are reviewed by the Regional Board, and there is a high degree of
  concern regarding estimated costs at the state level since all cities are in the same
  position as far as how to fund these requirements.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN commented that the cost would be astronomical to
  cities. He then thanked Ms. McGowan for her continued assistance on this
  matter. Ms. McGowan noted that she will pursue funding wherever she can.

  In response to MAYOR ZUCKERMAN, Ms. McGowan noted that importing of
  highly treated wastewater is a possible alternative to improving water quality at
  Lake Machado.

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL, Ms. McGowan noted that the
  Sanitation Districts may be able to assist cities with engineering resources.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL

  TO APPROVE THE PROFESSIONAL SERVICES AGREEMENT WITH
  MC GOWAN CONSULTING LLC FOR MS4 PERMIT COMPLIANCE
  ASSISTANCE FOR FY 2016-17 IN AN AMOUNT NOT TO EXCEED $88,800.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
JUNE 28, 2016
 D.  AWARD OF BID – STORM DRAIN CLEANING AND VIDEO INSPECTION

  Recommendation: That the City Council award the bid to Sancon Engineering,
  Inc., to provide cleaning, condition assessment and closed-circuit television
  (CCTV) inspection services on 76 high priority storm drain pipes in the amount of
  $43,500, plus $225 per hour for any pipes that require heaving cleaning.

  Assistant City Manager Grammer provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  In response to COUNCILWOMAN HUFF, Assistant City Manager Grammer noted
  that the hourly rate would be imposed on a case-by-case basis where extensive
  cleaning is needed.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL thanked City Attorney Davis for his assistance on
  this project.

  City Attorney Davis thanked Assistant City Manager Grammer for his creative
  thinking as well.

  City Manager Prichard commented that this solution is an example of the positive
  relationship the City continues to maintain with the County.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL also thanked Assistant City Manager Grammer.

  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO AWARD THE BID TO SANCON ENGINEERING, INC., TO PROVIDE
  CLEANING,  CONDITION  ASSESSMENT  AND  CLOSED-CIRCUIT
  TELEVISION (CCTV) INSPECTION SERVICES ON 76 HIGH PRIORITY
  STORM DRAIN PIPES IN THE AMOUNT OF $43,500, PLUS $225 PER
  HOUR FOR ANY PIPES THAT REQUIRE HEAVY CLEANING.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Zerunyan, Zuckerman
  ABSENT:  Schmitz

10.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 18-16; PROPOSALS TO CONDUCT HYDROLOGY
  STUDY FOR DAPPLEGRAY LANES BRIDLE TRAIL, INCLUDING JUNE’S TRAIL AT
  PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST

  Recommendation: That the City Council: 1) Appoint a Council subcommittee to
  review the engineering hydrology proposals including holding interviews with one
  or more of the companies; or 2) Direct staff to bring back a Professional Services
  Agreement (PSA) to retain one of the following engineering companies: HRGreen,
  Transtech, or Willdan.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material).

  Extensive discussion ensued regarding the variation in quotes, and whether or
  not each entailed the entire scope of work.

  Planning Director Wahba commented that he was quite impressed with Transtech
  and has heard many positive comments about their work.

  MAYOR PRO TEM ZERUNYAN noted that he would be happy to negotiate with
  Transtech on behalf of the City in an effort to lower their cost.

  After further discussion, COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL moved, seconded by
  COUNCILWOMAN HUFF

  TO DIRECT STAFF TO BRING BACK AN AGREEMENT WITH TRANSTECH
  TO CONDUCT A HYDROLOGY STUDY FOR DAPPLEGRAY LANES BRIDLE
  TRAIL, INCLUDING JUNE’S TRAIL AT PALOS VERDES DRIVE EAST.

  THERE BEING NO OBJECTION MAYOR ZUCKERMAN SO ORDERED.

JUNE 28, 2016
 11.  CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

  City Attorney Davis to bring back a teleconferencing policy for COUNCIL review.

12.  CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS: This item provides the

B.  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL noted that the SCAG Regional Transportation Plan

  California Contract Cities Association will be retiring. He announced that Marcel

  MAYOR ZUCKERMAN suggested sending a letter to Mr. Olivito congratulating him
  on his retirement.

D.  COUNCILWOMAN MITCHELL reported that the Metro Board voted to place the
  Measure R (sales tax) proposal on the November ballot.

E.  City Manager Prichard announced the upcoming retirement of Chris McKenzie,
  Executive Director of the League of California Cities.

13.  MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS: This item provides the opportunity for Members
  of the City Council to request information on currently pending projects and/or
  issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future consideration

A.  APPOINTMENT OF MEDIAN LANDSCAPE SUBCOMMITTEE

  Community Services Director Clark provided a brief update noting that staff has
  received Statements of Qualifications and a subcommittee is requested to be
  formed to interview the firms. He noted that Park and Activities Commissioner
